title: DfE Decoded 166 The PE and Sport Premium Has Changed
author: Paul Urry
summary: Paul Urry walks school leaders through the 2026/27 conditions of grant for the PE and Sport Premium, which bring a new funding formula, a single payment and tighter expectations. He frames a bigger leadership question underneath the guidance: after a decade of funding, the money should leave the school better at delivering PE after it is spent, not simply keep the offer running. The new formula pays £6,240 plus £10 per pupil for schools with 17 or more eligible pupils, which means a typical two-form primary receives around £9,840. The full allocation must be spent by 31 July 2027 with no carry-forward or prepayment. Urry stresses that the premium cannot cover PPA time, ordinary curriculum PE, core swimming or most salaries, capital spending or staff kit, and that external coaches should build teacher capability rather than substitute for teachers.
points: The funding formula has changed to £6,240 plus £10 per pupil for most schools, which will mean a lower allocation for many and makes spending choices more important.
The whole allocation arrives in one payment and must be spent by 31 July 2027, with no carry-forward and no prepaying for next year's services.
The premium must build capacity and capability in the school, so it should fund enhancement rather than substitute for core budget responsibilities.
Using the premium to pay coaches or specialists to cover PPA, deliver ordinary curriculum PE or cover lessons does not meet the conditions.
Capital expenditure, staff PE kit and statutory swimming lessons are excluded, although revenue maintenance such as repainting playground markings may be allowed.
quotes: This should not simply be money that keeps the PE offer running. It should leave the school better at delivering PE and sport after the money has been spent.
Schools must spend the entire 2026/27 allocation by 31 July 2027. Unused funding cannot be rolled forward.
The funding should make the school more capable. Better trained staff. Stronger subject leadership. More sustainable provision.

The PE and Sport Premium cannot be used to employ coaches or specialist teachers to cover planning, preparation and assessment time. Nor can it be used simply to fund delivery of the existing PE curriculum.
That means leaders need to be very clear about the distinction between enhancement and substitution.
The premium is additional funding. It should fund additional improvement. Not replace the normal school budget.
More opportunities that can continue. That is a very different principle from simply paying someone else to deliver PE for a year.
